analysis.one_line_summary: A creator styles her frizzy, curly hair with the Wavytalk thermal brush while debunking myths about heat damage on curly hair.
analysis.full_description: A young female creator demonstrates the Wavytalk Blowout Boost thermal round brush on her thick, curly, frizzy brunette hair. She begins with half of her hair styled straight and smooth, and proceeds to debunk misconceptions about heat styling curly hair. She explains her hair care routine (heat protectant, detangling, small sections, and negative ionic technology), shows how she styles sections of her hair including the crown and front fringe, and finishes by showing her voluminous blowout result while encouraging viewers to check the shopping cart link.

analysis.transcript_full_original: So many people get so mad whenever I say that you actually can heat style naturally curly hair without damaging it. I've been heat styling my hair two if not three times a week for the past two years, and I have not noticed any damage, but I do it the right way. First, I never skip heat protection no matter what, and I always use small sections and detangle those sections before going in with any hot tool so there's less room for damage like pulling on my hair. Next, all the hot tools I use have negative ionic technology that helps protect against heat damage, like this brush from Wavytalk. It's their Blowout Boost. It also has negative ionic technology. I'm honestly sick of the fear-mongering on social media that if you straighten or blow out your hair once, you're going to have horrible damage and your curl pattern is never going to be the same, and that is simply not true. At the end of the day, if you're diffusing your hair, that's using heat, or if you're using like a styling brush, that's using tension. So it really does not matter, just use everything in moderation. So don't let anybody make you feel bad for heat styling your curls every now and then. I honestly prefer a blowout over just straightened hair, so that's why I love to use this brush, because it gives me a gorgeous blowout without having to use a hair dryer and a round brush. And there you have it, here's the finished hair. You can in fact heat style your natural curls without being worried about them being damaged. But I do highly recommend making the switch to a tool that uses negative ionic technology, whether you get this one or a different one. But if you want to try out my tried and true, it's linked down below in the orange shopping cart with all of the different cute color options.
